<<<
Session Chair's Sheet — Room 2B, Thursday morning

One room, one projector, one lapel pack, one AV desk, one chair. Three talks, thirty minutes each, with questions after every one. The chair calls each speaker to the lectern; nothing starts until they do.

Before the room opens
Line check at the AV desk: laptop, HDMI, house sound, record feed. 30 minutes.
Test the projector once the desk is up: resolution, keystone, the cue slide. 15 minutes.
Check the lapel pack after the projector: battery, gain, a walk to the back row. 10 minutes.

Slides
Load the first deck once the lapel pack is checked; 10 minutes, and leave it on the cue slide.
Load the second deck as soon as the first talk's questions are over; 5 minutes.
Load the third deck while the coffee is going out; 5 minutes.

The session
Chair opens the room, housekeeping and fire exits; 5 minutes.
First talk when the chair calls the first speaker: 30 minutes.
Questions after the first talk: five to ten minutes, seven is the plan.
Changeover to the second speaker: unclip the pack, clip it on, 5 minutes.
Second talk when the chair calls the second speaker: 30 minutes.
Questions after the second talk: five to ten minutes, seven is the plan.
Changeover to the third speaker once the coffee is cleared from the foyer; 5 minutes.
Third talk when the chair calls the third speaker: 30 minutes.
Questions after the third talk: five to fifteen minutes, ten is the plan.
Chair closes the session; 5 minutes.

Catering
Set the coffee station in the service corridor from ninety minutes in; 30 minutes.
Coffee goes out to the foyer when the second talk's questions end; 20 minutes.
Clear the foyer; 10 minutes.

Strike
Strike the AV desk when the chair closes; 20 minutes, cables coiled, record feed off.

Notes
The projector is the contended thing, not the room: a deck cannot be loaded while a talk is on it, so every load sits in a gap. The lapel pack is the other one, and it is the reason changeovers are real steps rather than slack. Question time is the only elastic in the morning; if the first two run long the chair trims the third.
>>>

T1 read-back.source:
Source text (read all of it):
<<<
Product Launch Evening: Run of Show

Venue: the main hall, 200 seats, one stage with a single projector and a two-microphone PA, and a foyer with a bar. Crew: one producer calling the show, one AV technician, two front-of-house staff and the caterers. Crew call is 5:00 pm, doors are scheduled for 6:00 pm, and the program must be over by 8:00 pm so the reception can run before the venue resets at 9:00 pm.

Pre-show
The AV technician runs a full line check of the projector, clicker and both microphones; allow 30 minutes. The producer then walks the CEO and the product lead through the stage for a 20-minute rehearsal of the keynote transitions. Meanwhile front-of-house sets up the registration desk and lays out name badges, which takes 45 minutes, then does a 15-minute walkthrough of the foyer and the seating. Catering sets the bar and the canapé stations in the foyer over 60 minutes.

Doors
Doors open on the producer's call, not before front-of-house confirms the walkthrough is done. Guests arrive and register over 30 minutes while a welcome playlist runs in the hall and the bar serves drinks. When registration closes, front-of-house ushers guests to their seats, which takes 5 minutes.

Program
The host opens the program as soon as the hall is seated and welcomes the audience for 5 minutes. The CEO keynote begins on the host's cue and runs 20 minutes; the AV technician brings up the deck. Straight after the keynote the technician plays a 2-minute product video from the booth, and the product lead follows with a 25-minute live demo. A moderated Q&A follows for about 20 minutes, no less than 15 and no more than 25; the moderator closes it when the questions run dry or the clock says so. When the moderator hands back, the host closes the program in 5 minutes and invites everyone to the reception.

Reception
The foyer bar reopens as soon as the host closes, and catering circulates canapés for 45 minutes. Front-of-house breaks down the registration desk once the last guests have left the hall, about 15 minutes, and the AV technician strikes the stage over 30 minutes after the hall is clear.
>>>

T1 read-back.source:
Source text (read all of it):
<<<
HIIT Circuit Card — three athletes, four stations

Small group session, forty-five minutes on the clock including the warm-up and the stretch. There is one rower, one kettlebell, one box and one sled in the corner of the gym, and three of you. That means one station sits empty every round, and it means nobody ever waits on equipment if the rotation is respected.

The rule
Sixty seconds of work, all out, then sixty seconds of rest. Nobody starts a station until the athlete ahead of them has left it. If you are early, stand at the station and breathe; do not start.

Warm-up
Five minutes on the floor together: skipping, hip openers, shoulder pass-throughs, two sets of ten air squats. All three of you start at the same time and finish at the same time.

The stations
Rower: damper on five, pull hard, do not chase the split on the last ten seconds.
Kettlebell swings: one bell, hips not arms, chest tall at the top.
Box step-overs: alternate the lead leg, full extension at the top, no rebound.
Sled push: the length of the turf and back, low hands, short steps.

The rotation
Round 1: A on the rower, B on the kettlebell, C on the box.
Round 2: A on the kettlebell, B on the box, C on the sled.
Round 3: A on the box, B on the sled, C on the rower.
Round 4: A on the sled, B on the rower, C on the kettlebell.

Rest
Sixty seconds of rest on the floor after every station. Walk it off, do not sit down, do not lean on the next piece of equipment while somebody is still using it. There is no rest after the fourth station: that one runs straight into the cooldown.

Cooldown
Ten minutes on the floor when all three of you have finished the fourth station: easy bike or a walk, then quads, hips and thoracic spine. Nobody leaves early; the cooldown starts together.

Coach's note
The sled is the one that wrecks the rotation if somebody drags it. It is the longest reset and it is at the far end of the turf, so the athlete coming off the sled is the one most likely to hold up the person behind them. Watch that hand-off.
>>>

T1 read-back.source:
Source text (read all of it):
<<<
Partner Upper-Body Superset Session

Two lifters, one flat bench with a barbell, one pair of dumbbells, one pull-up bar and two rowing ergs. The whole session should take about 25 minutes. You work as a pair: while Partner A is on the first exercise of a superset, Partner B is on the second, and then you swap; nobody waits for equipment if you keep the order.

Warm-up
Both partners start together with 5 minutes of easy rowing on the ergs, followed by 3 minutes of arm circles and band pull-aparts.

Superset A: bench press and dumbbell row (2 rounds)
Partner A loads the bar and does a set of 8 bench presses, which takes about 40 seconds. Partner B starts on the dumbbell row at the same time, 8 per side, also about 40 seconds. Then swap: A goes to the rows once B has finished with the dumbbells, and B takes the bench as soon as A racks the bar. After both exercises, rest 90 seconds before the next round. Do 2 rounds, resting after each.

Superset B: overhead press and pull-ups (2 rounds)
Move straight on after the last rest. Partner A does 8 strict overhead presses with the dumbbells, about 45 seconds, while Partner B does a set of pull-ups, 6 to 10 reps, about 30 seconds. Swap when both are done: A moves to the pull-up bar, and B takes the dumbbells when A sets them down. Rest 2 minutes between rounds; there is no rest after the second round.

Cool-down
Finish together with 5 minutes of stretching: doorway chest stretch, lat stretch on the pull-up bar, and slow shoulder rolls.
>>>

T1 read-back.source:
Source text (read all of it):
<<<
Backyard Barbecue: Smoker and Grill

Two cooks, one offset smoker, one kettle grill, one side burner and a cooler for holding. The pork owns the smoker all day; everything else happens in the last two hours.

Pork shoulder
Light the smoker and bring it to 250°F; 45 minutes. While it comes up, trim the shoulder and rub it heavily with salt, pepper and paprika; 25 minutes. Put the shoulder on once the smoker holds temperature and smoke it unwrapped for 6 hours, until the bark is dark and set. Wrap it tightly in butcher paper; 10 minutes. Back on the smoker, wrapped, until the thickest part probes soft — usually another 3 hours, sometimes four. Hold it wrapped in a cooler for one to three hours; it will not get cold and it only gets better. Pull the meat by hand; 30 minutes.

Beans
When the pork goes into the cooler, fry the bacon and onion in the pot on the side burner for 12 minutes, then add the beans, molasses and a ladle of drippings and let them tick over on the lowest flame until you serve.

Slaw
Start the slaw at the same time. Shred the cabbage and carrot; 20 minutes. Whisk the buttermilk dressing; 8 minutes. Dress the slaw and put it in the refrigerator for at least 45 minutes so the cabbage softens.

Grill
Light the kettle an hour before you eat; 25 minutes to a clean bed of coals. Grill the sausages for 14 minutes. Grill the corn for 10 minutes. Toast the buns for 3 minutes, last, so they stay warm.

Table
Set out plates, pickles and sauce once the buns are off; 10 minutes. Call everyone over when both cooks say it is ready; 5 minutes to lay it all out.
>>>

Source text (read all of it):
<<<
Country Loaf: Two Boules, One Dutch Oven

One batch of dough, two loaves, and a single dutch oven that has to bake them one after the other. One oven, one baker, one refrigerator. Times count from eight in the morning; the loaves come out of the fridge the next day.

Levain
Mix 50 g of ripe starter with 100 g of flour and 100 g of water in a jar; 5 minutes. Leave the jar at room temperature until it domes and smells sweet, 4 to 6 hours.

Dough
Weigh the flour, water and salt for the whole bake first thing; 10 minutes. At half past eight, whisk 900 g of flour into 680 g of water; 5 minutes. Let it autolyse for 1 hour. When the levain is ripe, squeeze it into the autolysed dough with 20 g of salt and work it by hand for 10 minutes. Bulk ferment at 24°C until the dough has risen by half, 3 to 5 hours. Fold the dough in the bowl half an hour after mixing, again half an hour later, and a third time after another half hour; each fold takes 2 minutes.

Divide and shape
Tip the dough out, cut it in two and preshape each piece into a loose round; 10 minutes. Let the rounds rest on the bench for 25 minutes. Shape both boules tightly and settle them into floured bannetons; 10 minutes. Retard them in the refrigerator, 10 to 14 hours.

Bake
Three quarters of an hour before the dough comes out, put the dutch oven in the oven and heat both to 250°C. Score the first loaf and lower it in; 3 minutes. Bake the first loaf covered for 20 minutes, then uncover it and bake for another 20 minutes until the crust is dark. Cool it on a rack for at least an hour before cutting. Re-heat the empty dutch oven for 10 minutes. Score the second loaf and lower it in; 3 minutes. Bake the second loaf covered for 20 minutes, then uncover it for a final 20 minutes. Cool the second loaf on the rack beside the first.
>>>

T1 read-back.source:
Source text (read all of it):
<<<
Passaging Two Flasks of Adherent HEK293 Cells

Two T75 flasks at about 90 % confluence are split 1:6 into four new flasks. The room has one biosafety cabinet, one 37 °C water bath, one CO₂ incubator, one benchtop centrifuge and one microscope with a haemocytometer. Only one flask can be open in the cabinet at a time, so the two flasks queue for it while the centrifuge and the microscope stay free. Work with pre-warmed medium, PBS and trypsin-EDTA throughout; nothing cold touches the cells. One operator.

Preparation
1. Wipe down the cabinet, lay out pipettes and tubes, and let the blower run; 10 minutes.
2. Check both flasks on the microscope for confluence and contamination; 10 minutes.

Flask A
3. Aspirate the spent medium and rinse the monolayer with 5 mL of PBS; 4 minutes in the cabinet.
4. Add 2 mL of trypsin-EDTA, rock the flask and return it to the incubator for 5 minutes.
5. Knock the flask, check detachment and neutralise with 8 mL of medium; 5 minutes in the cabinet.
6. Transfer the suspension to a 15 mL tube and spin at 300 × g for 5 minutes.
7. Aspirate the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 10 mL of fresh medium; 4 minutes.
8. Count the cells on the haemocytometer; 6 minutes.
9. Seed two new T75 flasks at 1:6 and label them; 6 minutes in the cabinet.
10. Return the new flasks to the incubator and leave them to settle overnight, at least 16 hours.

Flask B
11. Start flask B the moment flask A leaves the cabinet: aspirate and rinse with 5 mL of PBS; 4 minutes.
12. Trypsinise flask B in the incubator for 5 minutes.
13. Neutralise flask B as soon as flask A is out of the cabinet again; 5 minutes.
14. Spin flask B at 300 × g for 5 minutes once the centrifuge is free.
15. Resuspend the flask B pellet in 10 mL of fresh medium; 4 minutes.
16. Count flask B on the haemocytometer once flask A has been counted; 6 minutes.
17. Seed two more T75 flasks at 1:6 and label them; 6 minutes.
18. Return them to the incubator to settle overnight alongside the first pair.

Finishing
19. Wipe the cabinet down, discard the waste and switch the blower to standby; 10 minutes.
20. Write the passage number, the split ratio and the counts into the culture log; 5 minutes.
>>>
